purpose: Private claim-specific background receipts for the E01 beginner lesson. These references support definitions and methodological framing; the run manifest and stamped phase files support the empirical numbers.

E01_METHOD_METRICS.citation: Goldberg and Mahmoud, Drawdown: From Practice to Theory and Back Again (2014), plus the series diagnostic boundary
E01_METHOD_METRICS.locator: https://arxiv.org/abs/1404.7493; C:/Users/MSI/Desktop/Obsidian Vault From VPS/tradercockpit/tradercockpit/GTM/Social-Media-Library/Into the Laboratory — Production Standard.md:586-592
E01_METHOD_METRICS.supports: Maximum drawdown as a peak-to-trough risk measure and the warning that profit factor is one diagnostic rather than a verdict; the episode uses the recorded ratios only as development-window measurements.
E01_METHOD_METRICS.limitations: The paper discusses drawdown risk generally; it does not validate the Futures run, its thresholds, or the candidate example.

E01_METHOD_SELECTION.citation: White, A Reality Check for Data Snooping, Econometrica 68(5), 1097-1126 (2000)
E01_METHOD_SELECTION.supports: The selection-burden explanation: reusing a data set for inference or model selection creates a data-snooping problem, so the size of the searched candidate field belongs beside an attractive result.
E01_METHOD_SELECTION.limitations: This is methodological background; it does not establish that any particular E01 survivor is overfit.

E01_METHOD_PREREGISTRATION.citation: Open Science Framework, OSF Dictionary: Preregistrations
E01_METHOD_PREREGISTRATION.supports: The plain-English explanation that a preregistration is a study plan submitted before reviewing the data, with changes time-stamped and made transparent.
E01_METHOD_PREREGISTRATION.limitations: The receipt describes research transparency practice; it does not prove that this historical E01 run was preregistered.
